fields.meta_title: Roofing Landing Page for Inspections and Quotes | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A roofing landing page that books roof inspections and takes quote requests. See four roofer examples, from leak repairs to commercial bids.
fields.h1: Build a Roofing Landing Page That Books Inspections and Quotes
fields.hero_description: Get a roofing landing page where homeowners book an inspection or ask for a quote, and every request lands in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Roofing Page Needs Before the Visit
fields.features_subheading: Each part settles something a homeowner wants to know before handing over an address. Emergent builds all six from your prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A line on what happens after the button

Say under the button who calls back and by when, in words the office can keep, such as a call before noon the next day. Nobody who sends a request has to wonder what happens next.
fields.feature_2:
A time to pick instead of a message box

Offer the inspection as a day and a window instead of a blank box asking about the project. The homeowner leaves the page knowing when someone is coming to look at the roof.
fields.feature_3:
Quote questions the estimator asks anyway

Ask what covers the roof today and how tall the house is. With those two answers, the estimator can plan the visit, and bring the right ladder, before driving out to the house.
fields.feature_4:
Finished roofs from your own crews

Put photos of jobs your crews finished next to the form, and caption each with its town and material. A homeowner then pictures a roof a few streets away, not a stock photo.
fields.feature_5:
An email to the person who takes the job

Send each request to the estimator or crew lead who handles that kind of work, with the address and phone in the email. A request that matches no rule goes to one shared inbox.
fields.feature_6:
Every request saved in a database you own

Each booking and quote request saves as a row with the job type, the roof details, and the page it came from. Sort a season of jobs by material or by town, in a database you own.

fields.tab_content_1:
Chimney and skylight leaks: 14 of 26 this week

Glenrock Roofing's repair page asks where the water shows before the name: Ceiling stain, Attic, Chimney, or Skylight. Chimney and Skylight requests go to Dario Pellis, who fixes flashing, and the rest go to the repair crew. This week 26 repair requests came in: 14 for Dario and 12 for the crew.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two inspection windows a day, picked by the homeowner

Copper Hollow Roofing books roof inspections on the page itself. The homeowner picks a weekday, then Morning or Afternoon, and the booking lands on the list of Wren Albright, the company's inspector, with the address at the top. This week 31 inspections were booked: 19 for a morning and 12 for an afternoon.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every metal roof quote goes past the shingle team

Pikeford Roof Co. asks which roof the homeowner wants and the number of stories before it asks for the address. Metal roof requests go to Ines Corrado, the estimator who prices metal, so the shingle team never sees them. This month 40 quote requests came in: 9 for metal and 31 for the shingle team.
fields.tab_content_4:
For bids over 20,000 square feet, the owner reads first

Osterly Commercial Roofing asks property managers for the building type and the roof size in square feet. A bid over 20,000 square feet emails the owner, Maren Ostby, before an estimator sees it, and smaller roofs go straight to the estimators. This quarter 6 of 22 bid requests were that large.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Roofing Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a roofing landing page that books inspections and sends each quote request to the estimator who prices it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Give each job its own page
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the headline in the ad's words
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put a call button on the first screen
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Name who gets each kind of request
fields.howto_step_1_des: Point the leak repair ad at a repair page and the replacement ad at a quote page. A homeowner with water on the ceiling wants someone out this week, not a chart of shingle colors.
fields.howto_step_2_des: If the ad says roof leak repair, the headline says roof leak repair too. The visitor sees at once that the click landed on the right page and keeps reading.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Some homeowners want to talk, not type. Show the office number as a button they can tap, near the top, and repeat it next to the form for anyone who scrolls.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List every job in your prompt with the person who takes it: leaks to the repair lead, metal quotes to the metal estimator, large roofs to the owner. Emergent builds the routing from that list.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask only what you price from
fields.howto_step_5_des: Think through your estimator's last few phone calls and keep the questions asked on every one. Cut anything that gets asked again on the call anyway. A short form is a form that gets finished.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Check it on a phone, outdoors
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the page on a phone while standing outside, the way a homeowner looking up at a drip would. The headline and the call button belong on the first screen, with the first field right below.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit one request of each kind from your own phone. Check that each email reaches the right person and that every test shows up in the table before you pay for the first click.

faq_plan.q: What is a roofing landing page?
faq_plan.a: A roofing landing page is one page built for one roofing job, such as a leak repair or a replacement quote. It ends in a single action: an inspection booking or a quote request. It carries no site menu to wander off through, and every ad for that job points to it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a roofing landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder in plain English, naming the job it books and who should get each request. Emergent builds the page, its form, and the database behind it, and you change any part by prompting. Send one test request of each kind before the ads go live.

faq_plan.q: What should a roofing landing page show before the form?
faq_plan.a: Show the job in the headline, the towns you work in, and a photo of a roof your crew finished, all before the first field. Add a call button for homeowners who want to talk instead. Keep reviews to two or three short quotes that name the job.

faq_plan.q: How is a roofing landing page different from a roofing website?
faq_plan.a: A roofing website explains the whole company, while a landing page does one job for one ad and leaves out the menu. Keep the website for the homeowner who is still comparing roofers, and send paid clicks to the page. An automotive landing page splits the same way, with one page for a service special and the dealer's site for browsing.

faq_plan.q: Should a roofing landing page offer free inspections?
faq_plan.a: Offer one only if your inspectors can keep up with the bookings it brings in. Say on the page what the visit covers and how long it takes. The homeowner then knows what to expect at the door. If inspections carry a fee, state the fee next to the button instead of leaving it for the phone call.

faq_plan.q: What photos should a roofing landing page use?
faq_plan.a: Use photos of roofs your own crews finished, taken from the street the way a neighbor would see them. Caption each one with its town and the material, and put one beside the form. Skip stock photos of smiling roofers, since a real job a few streets away is the one a homeowner can go and look at.

faq_plan.q: Should metal roofs get a separate roofing landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you sell metal roofs as a separate line with its own estimator. Treat it the way you would a product launch landing page: one offer, the questions that price it, and a single button. Emergent changes the page by prompting, and the metal page can start as a copy of the shingle page with new questions.

faq_plan.q: Where do the requests from a roofing landing page go?
faq_plan.a: On a page Emergent builds, each request saves as a row in a database you own, with the job type and the roof details in their own columns. The app can also send each one to the tool your office already uses, since built apps connect to any tool with an API. Pick one place the office checks first, and keep it the same for every page.

faq_plan.q: Can I start from a roofing landing page template?
faq_plan.a: Yes, and a template is a fine start if its form asks the questions your estimator prices from. Check that the fields, the photos, and the routing fit your jobs before you publish. On Emergent you describe the page instead of filling in a template, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: Should a roofing landing page book inspections by exact time or by window?
faq_plan.a: Offer windows, such as morning or afternoon, unless your inspectors keep to the minute. A roof visit runs long when the inspector finds something, and a window gives the next homeowner an honest arrival time. A dentist landing page can offer exact slots because every visit happens in the same chair, while a roof inspector drives between houses.

plan.angle: Searchers for roofing landing page get agency checklists, template galleries and design showcases that show what a roofer's page looks like, never what happens to an inspection booking or a quote request after the homeowner taps the button. This page shows four roofing landing pages built around those two jobs (a leak repair form that asks where the water shows, an inspection page with morning and afternoon windows, a replacement quote form that routes metal roofs to their own estimator, a commercial bid page that sends large roofs to the owner), each with the form, the routing and the saved row behind it, then gives the build steps a roofer needs. It makes no insurance-claim, building-code, warranty, material-lifespan or state-specific claims. HVAC, contractor, solar and plumber pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
